title.narrative: Through UNICEF’s upstream support, the enabling environment for sanitation and hygiene was strengthened by improving national monitoring systems, updating policies and guidelines, and driving high-level advocacy through the Kenya Sanitation Alliance of 15 high-burden counties. Downstream, 2,019 villages were certified open defecation-free, and 445,204 people gained access to at least basic sanitation services, including 209,484 in urban informal settlements with safely managed sanitation. Additionally, 677,060 people gained access to basic hand hygiene facilities. In humanitarian contexts, 719,698 were reached with hygiene promotion and cholera prevention messages, and 53,473 gained access to emergency sanitation services.
